sources.label: Transport for NSW - trip planner & timetables
Transport for NSW - Opal & contactless payments

blocks.text: Catch a T4 train to Bondi Junction, then the 333 or 380 bus down to Campbell Parade, right across from the sand. From Circular Quay it's about 40-45 minutes all up - the bus leg itself is only around 15 minutes. There's no train station at the beach. Just tap on with any contactless card or phone - it costs the same as an Opal card.

There's no train station at the beach itself (a common surprise for first-timers), so nearly every public-transport route funnels through Bondi Junction first. Here's exactly how I'd do it, whether you're coming from the CBD, the airport, or driving in for the day.

From the city, take a T4 Eastern Suburbs line train to Bondi Junction - the end of the line and a big interchange. Follow the signs down to the bus stands: two routes run to the beach, the 333 (from Stand A at Bondi Junction) and the 380. The 333 is the one I aim for - mid-morning it's coming every few minutes. Either way, get off at Campbell Parade (the Stand C stop) and the sand is right across the road. Check the Transport for NSW trip planner for live times before you set off.

The 333 also runs all the way from the CBD (Circular Quay through to Bondi Beach), so if you'd rather stay on one bus the whole way you can skip the train entirely. It's slower than train-then-bus, but you get the harbour-to-ocean view for the trouble.

On a hot summer weekend, the bus down from Bondi Junction can crawl and fill up fast. If it's a gorgeous day and you're able, the walk from Bondi Junction to the beach is roughly 25–30 minutes downhill - sometimes genuinely quicker than waiting for a packed bus, and a nice way to arrive.

You don't need a paper ticket, and drivers don't sell them. Just tap on with an Opal card or any contactless card or phone (Apple Pay, Google Pay and the like) as you board, and tap off again as you get out - buses charge by distance, so skipping the tap-off costs you the maximum fare. Opal cards are sold at convenience stores, supermarkets and stations if you'd prefer one, but for most visitors the card already in your pocket is the easiest option. Fares are distance-based with daily and weekly caps - check Transport for NSW for the current amounts before you travel.

blocks.title: Coming from Sydney Airport?
blocks.text: Take the train from the airport to Central, then change to a T4 train to Bondi Junction, and finish on the 333 or 380 bus down to Bondi Beach. Note the airport stations charge an extra station-access fee on top of the normal fare - an airport thing, not a Bondi thing. I've written up every option, fees and all, in [our airport guide](/bondi-blog/getting-from-sydney-airport-to-bondi-beach).

Driving is easy enough - Bondi sits only a handful of kilometres east of the CBD - but I'll be honest about parking, because it's the catch. There's metered street parking around Campbell Parade and the surrounding streets plus a car park behind the beach, but on any warm weekend it fills early and you'll be circling. The metered spots are paid and time-limited, so read the signs carefully and check current rates and time limits with Waverley Council.

If you're set on driving in summer, get there early or you'll spend your morning hunting for a space. Better yet, park at Bondi Junction and bus or walk down - it saves the beachfront scramble entirely.

Uber, taxis and other rideshare services all serve Bondi and will take you door to sand. It's the most convenient option if you're carrying gear or travelling as a group, though fares climb with demand - expect to pay noticeably more on hot afternoons and event weekends.

items.q: Is there a train station at Bondi Beach?
items.a: No. The closest station is Bondi Junction on the T4 line, a few kilometres uphill from the sand. From there you take the 333 or 380 bus down (the 333 leaves from Stand A) or walk in roughly 25-30 minutes.

items.q: Which bus goes to Bondi Beach?
items.a: Two routes: the 333, which runs all the way from Circular Quay via Bondi Junction (Stand A at the interchange), and the 380 from Watsons Bay via Bondi Junction. Both drop you on Campbell Parade at the beach - check the Transport for NSW trip planner for today's times.

items.q: Do I need an Opal card, or can I tap my phone?
items.a: Either works. You can tap on with a physical Opal card or with a contactless bank card or phone wallet - same fares and the same daily caps. On buses, tap on as you board and tap off as you get out - fares are distance-based, so missing the tap-off charges you the maximum fare.

items.q: How long does it take to get to Bondi from the city?
items.a: Allow roughly 40-45 minutes from Circular Quay, by train-then-bus (the one-seat 333 ride is similar but usually a little slower) - longer on busy summer weekends when traffic and crowds slow the buses down. Check Transport for NSW's trip planner for live times.

items.q: Is it worth driving to Bondi Beach?
items.a: Only if you arrive early. Parking is metered, time-limited and fills fast on warm days. Public transport is usually the less stressful choice - or park at Bondi Junction and finish the trip by bus.

blocks.text: However you come, my advice is the same: travel light, go early on a summer weekend, and let the bus or train do the work. Bondi's genuinely one of the easiest world-famous beaches to reach - the hardest part is leaving.
